{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
file_path = 'data/sales.csv'
data = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Convert `revenue` from string with commas to float
data['revenue_numeric'] = data['revenue'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False).astype(float)

# Identify QA orders (revenue == 999999.99)
qa_orders = data[data['revenue_numeric'] == 999999.99]

# Check if any QA orders are in the group of NEW customers reached by PAID SEARCH
filtered_qa = qa_orders[(qa_orders['channel'] == 'paid_search') & (qa_orders['customer_segment'] == 'new')]
print(f'Number of QA orders among NEW customers reached by PAID SEARCH: {len(filtered_qa)}')

# Since it's 0, the QA orders do not affect the current group
# Therefore, even though they exist in the dataset, they are not in the subgroup of interest
# So, the conversion rate computation for NEW customers in PAID SEARCH is unaffected

# Now, proceed with the original calculation
filtered_data = data[(data['channel'] == 'paid_search') & (data['customer_segment'] == 'new')]
converted_count = filtered_data['converted'].sum()
total_count = len(filtered_data)
conversion_rate = converted_count / total_count

# Print the final value
conversion_rate"}
